answer: An agent economy resists sybils with trust-graph random walks: honest agents vouch only for partners they have really worked with, anchoring trust in verified seed identities. Walks start from those seeds, and influence equals each agent's visit-probability share. A sybil operator can mint a thousand cheap ids, an island of impostors, yet connects to the honest graph through only a few bridge edges, so walks rarely arrive. One genuine vouch is cheap as a quill stroke; a velvet web of fakes costs real social capital per bridge edge.
